# Build and Release Guide

This guide applies to the `dev` branch of the Kawaikara repository.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22 or newer.
- pnpm 10 or newer. The repository pins pnpm `10.33.0` in `package.json`.
- The local KawaiUI package expected by `@kawaikara/kawai-ui: link:../../KawaiUi`.
- Platform tools required by electron-builder for the target operating system.
- Castlabs EVS access for Widevine VMP-signed distributable builds.
- Apple Silicon native Video builds require libmpv headers and libraries from
  Homebrew's `/opt/homebrew` prefix. `MPV_INCLUDE_DIR`, `MPV_LIB`, and
  `MPV_RUNTIME_DIR` can override those paths.
- Windows x64 native Video builds require a libmpv development runtime below
  `%USERPROFILE%\libmpv` or the same `MPV_*` overrides.

Intel macOS and other unsupported libmpv targets intentionally skip the native
add-on build and package the Chromium/HLS compatibility backend instead.

Install workspace dependencies:

```bash
pnpm install
```

The app uses Castlabs Electron `40.10.6+wvcus`. This keeps Widevine support on the runtime already validated for Kawaikara's media and audio paths. At runtime, startup waits for the Widevine component before creating the viewer so DRM sites do not race CDM installation.

## Environment file

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill the Castlabs credentials when packaging DRM-capable builds:

```dotenv
KAWAIKARA_EVS_ACCOUNT=your-castlabs-account
KAWAIKARA_EVS_PASSWORD="your-castlabs-password"
```

The scripts first honor `KAWAIKARA_EVS_PYTHON` and
`KAWAIKARA_EVS_CONDA_ENV`, then inspect the active virtual/Conda environment,
project `.venv-evs` and `.venv` directories, the conventional Conda environment
named `vmp`, and available system Python commands. Optional overrides are useful
when EVS is installed elsewhere. `.env.local` is private and must not be
committed.

One supported local setup is:

```bash
conda create -n vmp python=3.10
conda run -n vmp python -m pip install castlabs-evs
```

Both account and password must be present together. Packaging scripts reject a half-configured credential pair.

## Development commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm dev` | Build packages/app in development mode and start Electron |
| `pnpm build:packages` | Build `site-api`, then `builtin-sites` |
| `pnpm build:app` | Production webpack build for Main, Preload, and Renderer |
| `pnpm build` | Build workspace packages and the production app bundle |
| `pnpm start` | Build and launch Electron |
| `pnpm typecheck` | Type-check packages, app, and Storybook |

Webpack emits:

```text
dist/
├── main/main.js
├── preload/
│   ├── preload.js
│   └── viewer.js
└── renderer/
    ├── index.html + overlay.js
    ├── video.html + video.js
    └── external-login.html + external-login.js
```

Build-time constants include the release channel and optional Discord application ID. Set `DISCORD_APP_ID` before building to enable Discord Rich Presence; an empty value disables it without failing startup.

## Storybook

Run the app-owned view and component catalog without Electron:

```bash
pnpm storybook
```

Storybook listens on port `6006`, loads KawaiUI and renderer styles, and installs `stories/Mocks/KawaikaraMock.ts` before each story. Stories currently cover Menu, Preference, Video, developer links, external-login status, update-panel states, PiP controls, site menu controls, and the downloader panel.

Create a static Storybook build with:

```bash
pnpm storybook:build
```

## Development package

```bash
pnpm package:dev
```

The script:

1. Requires the current `Kawaikara Dev` application to be stopped on macOS.
2. Authenticates EVS when credentials are configured.
3. Runs the development build.
4. Packages the current platform/architecture through `electron-builder.dev.config.cjs`.
5. Replaces the managed output atomically and restores the previous build if packaging fails.
6. On macOS and Windows, opens the packaged application once so the OS registers `kawaikara://`.

Development output is placed below:

```text
builds/dev/<os>/<arch>/
```

The development package uses app ID `day.faby.kawaikara.dev` and product name `Kawaikara Dev`. macOS certificate auto-discovery is disabled for this local package, but Widevine VMP signing still runs when `KAWAIKARA_VMP_SIGN=1`.

Verify the package signature and Widevine VMP state with:

```bash
pnpm widevine:verify
```

Authenticate EVS explicitly with:

```bash
pnpm widevine:auth
```

## Release channels

Kawaikara has three build/update channels:

| Build channel | Version shape | Updater channel | GitHub release type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stable | `3.0.0` | `latest` | Release |
| Staging | `3.0.0-staging.YYYYMMDD.RUN.ATTEMPT.gSHA` | `staging` | Prerelease |
| Nightly | `3.0.0-nightly.YYYYMMDD.RUN.ATTEMPT.gSHA` | `nightly` | Prerelease |

The package script temporarily changes `package.json` to the calculated release version, builds/packages, and restores the original file in a `finally` block.

The build number defaults to `GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`, or `0` outside CI. `KAWAIKARA_RELEASE_VERSION` can supply an explicit valid version.

Stable publishing still accepts a `v3.0.0` tag or a manual workflow run. Staging and Nightly do not use source-repository tags:

- `.github/workflows/nightly.yaml` selects an immutable commit from `dev` every day at 00:00 KST. It can also be run manually.
- `.github/workflows/staging.yaml` is manual and defaults to the latest `dev` commit.
- A manually supplied source SHA is rejected unless it belongs to `dev`.
- The same source commit is not published twice unless `force` is selected.
- Release notes and `channel-source.json` record the exact source repository, branch, commit, and Actions run.

The generated releases are published to separate public repositories:

| Channel | Release repository | Anchor branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stable | `fabyday/kawaikara` | release tag target |
| Staging | `Kawaikara/kawaikara-staging` | `staging` |
| Nightly | `Kawaikara/kawaikara-nightly` | `nightly` |

### Site API releases

External Bundle projects do not resolve `@kawaikara/site-api` from the npm
registry. The stable contract is released independently with an immutable
`vX.Y.Z` Git tag and a prebuilt `.tgz` GitHub Release artifact in the dedicated
[`Kawaikara/kawai-site-api`](https://github.com/Kawaikara/kawai-site-api)
repository.

The API repository owns its source tag and `release.yaml`. Pushing a matching
tag, for example `v1.0.0`, validates the package, packs and tests an isolated
tarball, and attaches that tarball to a GitHub Release. No `NPM_TOKEN` is
required. `KawaiBundleTemplate` pins that immutable `.tgz`, so a fresh clone has
a reproducible API dependency without a local `link:` path or monorepo build.
The desktop repository no longer owns a Site API release tag or workflow.

The scheduled workflow file itself must exist on the source repository's default branch because GitHub only starts scheduled workflows from that branch. The workflow still checks out and validates `dev`, so merging the workflow definition into `main` does not make `main` a Nightly source. Staging is the beta-equivalent channel; there is intentionally no separate `beta` channel.

Development-channel publishing uses a GitHub App instead of long-lived personal
access tokens:

1. Create a GitHub App owned by `Kawaikara` with repository `Contents: Read and
   write` permission.
2. Install it with access limited to `kawaikara-staging` and
   `kawaikara-nightly`.
3. Store its Client ID as the Actions repository or organization variable
   `KAWAIKARA_RELEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID`.
4. Generate a private key and store the complete PEM value as the Actions
   secret `KAWAIKARA_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.

The workflow uses `actions/create-github-app-token@v3` to mint a repository-
scoped installation token for each job. Prepare receives read-only Contents
permission; publishing receives write permission. The action revokes each token
when its job finishes. `STAGING_RELEASE_TOKEN` and `NIGHTLY_RELEASE_TOKEN` are
no longer used.

Keep the existing EVS, signing certificate, and Discord secrets used by Stable
publishing.

Versioned release notes live under `CHANGELOG/<base-version>`. English and
Korean patch-note files are required; Japanese is optional. The workflow builds
the GitHub Release body from those files, and the in-app Update Notes view picks
the current app language with English fallback.

Stable versions may not contain a prerelease suffix. Staging and Nightly versions must begin with their corresponding prerelease name.

## Build-only and publish commands

| Channel | Build without publishing | Build and publish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stable | `pnpm dist:stable` | `pnpm release:stable` |
| Staging | `pnpm dist:staging` | `pnpm release:staging` |
| Nightly | `pnpm dist:nightly` | `pnpm release:nightly` |

Automatic tag-based publishing remains available for local/legacy use, but the GitHub workflow uses it only for Stable:

```bash
pnpm release:auto
```

All channel packaging commands set `KAWAIKARA_VMP_SIGN=1`, authenticate EVS when credentials are available, run the full build, and invoke electron-builder.

## Platform artifacts

Release output is grouped by channel and operating system:

```text
builds/<channel>/<os>/
```

Configured targets are:

- macOS: DMG and ZIP for x64 and arm64.
- Windows: NSIS installer and ZIP for x64.
- Linux: AppImage for x64 and arm64.

The artifact name includes product, version, channel, OS, architecture, and extension. The application registers the `kawaikara://` protocol.

## Update behavior

`electron-updater` is configured with automatic install-on-quit disabled. Automatic update checks are also disabled by default in Preferences.

Every package is permanently bound to its build channel and release repository. Stable only reads `latest` metadata from `fabyday/kawaikara`, Staging only reads `staging` metadata from `Kawaikara/kawaikara-staging`, and Nightly only reads `nightly` metadata from `Kawaikara/kawaikara-nightly`. The application does not permit cross-channel upgrades or downgrades.

Manual checks open the update overlay and report checking, update-available,
up-to-date, unsupported, or error states. A found update exposes a separate,
scrollable Update Notes view before the user starts the download.

Automatic startup checks remain completely hidden while checking and when no
release is available. Once a newer release is found, the download panel appears,
downloads immediately, and relaunches Kawaikara after the package is ready.
Update checks return `unsupported` in a non-packaged development run.

## Discord presence

If `DISCORD_APP_ID` was embedded during webpack build and a Discord client is available, startup publishes Kawaikara Rich Presence with project/Discord buttons and configured image asset keys. Failure to connect is non-fatal, and shutdown clears/destroys the client.

## Pre-release checklist

- `pnpm typecheck` succeeds.
- `pnpm storybook:build` succeeds.
- `pnpm build` succeeds from a clean dependency install.
- The packaged build passes `pnpm widevine:verify`.
- DRM playback is tested with isolated site profiles.
- Login popup and external-browser flows are tested with a real account.
- Unified PiP enters, moves, resizes, and restores focus on landscape and portrait video.
- File drop and HLS playback work in the internal Video view.
- The release version matches its channel rules.
- GitHub updater metadata and all intended artifacts are present before publishing to users.
